original_question: Do there exist connected bipartite graphs with exactly four distinct adjacency eigenvalues and more than four distinct valencies?
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Problem 3.7 (page 6): "Are there connected bipartite graphs with four distinct eigenvalues and more than four distinct valencies ?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target almost verbatim. It correctly asks an existence question, restricts to connected bipartite graphs, uses the adjacency spectrum, and asks for exactly four distinct eigenvalues together with more than four distinct valencies. This is precisely the open problem stated as Problem 3.7 in Section 3.2 (page 6).
missing_details: The paper is using the standard graph-theoretic convention that the graphs are finite simple unsigned graphs here, even though the surrounding survey is about signed graphs; that implicit scope should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation (Section 3.2, page 6).
To be fully self-contained, 'four distinct adjacency eigenvalues' should be stated as: the adjacency matrix A(G) has exactly four distinct eigenvalues (Problem 3.7, page 6).

To be fully self-contained, 'more than four distinct valencies' should be stated formally as: the set of vertex degrees {deg_G(v) : v in V(G)} has cardinality greater than 4; in this problem, 'valencies' means vertex degrees (Problem 3.7, page 6).

No ambient field/ring, homogeneity, or nilpotency assumptions are relevant to this problem; the only hidden conventions to surface are the graph class (finite simple connected bipartite graphs) and the operator (the adjacency matrix).
refined_question: Does there exist a finite simple connected bipartite graph G such that its adjacency matrix A(G) has exactly four distinct eigenvalues and the degree set {deg_G(v) : v in V(G)} has cardinality greater than 4?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 3.2 rather than a broader signed-graph problem. In the paper, the exact matching statement is Problem 3.7 on page 6. The immediately preceding sentence says that Van Dam, Koolen and Jia posed it as "the following bipartite version of De Caen's problem above," referring to Problem 3.6 in the same section and page. That nearby context shows the intended scope: an unsigned graph problem about connected bipartite graphs, adjacency eigenvalues, and vertex valencies, with no extra hypotheses and no stated equivalent reformulation. Because the draft already tracks the official wording very closely, the only needed refinement is to surface the implicit conventions that G is a finite simple graph, A(G) is the adjacency matrix, and valencies are vertex degrees.
